newsitem.title: INDONESIA: TIMAH SEES H2 NET IMPROVING OVER H1.
newsitem.headline: TIMAH SEES H2 NET IMPROVING OVER H1.

text.p: The world's largest integrated tin miner, Indonesia's PT Tambang Timah, expects net profit in the second half of the year to be higher than in the first six months, president director Erry Riana said on Thursday.
"The second-half results will be better than the first-half," he told Reuters, adding that the full-year net profit was likely to be the same as in 1996.
Timah posted net profit of 57.30 billion rupiah in the first six months of 1997 against 70.58 billion rupiah in the year-ago period.
It posted 156.6 billion rupiah net profit in 1996.
Riana said he was confident of an improved performance in the second half because of increases in international tin prices. He also said the company's exports were denominated in dollars.
The rupiah has plunged in recent weeks against the dollar.
Riana also said the company may have to adjust production levels to match demand, but refused to give details.
